description: Trace recursive calls in fibonacci(5) to see how branching into fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2) recomputes the same subproblems.

steps.description: Define fibonacci(int n) with two base cases: return 0 when n <= 0 (lines 3-4) and return 1 when n <= 2 (lines 5-6).
For n > 2, return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2) on line 8, and call fibonacci(5) from main on line 13.

steps.answer: fibonacci(5) calls fibonacci(4) and fibonacci(3), and fibonacci(4) also calls fibonacci(3) and fibonacci(2), so fibonacci(3) is computed twice from scratch.
steps.question: When main calls fibonacci(5), how many separate times is fibonacci(3) called?

steps.description: Follow the call stack down to the base case n <= 2 on line 6 as fibonacci(5) branches through n = 4, 3, and 2.

title: Overlapping Subproblems in Recursive Fibonacci
